supersedes: does not replace PREREGISTRATION.json (first pass) -- this is a SECOND, additive pre-registration for the fix pass, per the prompt's instruction
ordering_attestation: Written before any company was re-tested under the new rules and before any return was looked at. The justifications below (A1, A2) cite ONLY coverage/reporting-cadence mechanics -- never a company's outcome or return, and never a reference to which companies would be restored as a result of the rule change.

A1_gap_rule_days.rule: Replace the first pass's '2 consecutive quarters' gap test with a fixed 240-calendar-day threshold between consecutive earnings calls within the coverage window, for every stratum except S4 (S4 uses A2 instead).
A1_gap_rule_days.justification_coverage_only: Ordinary quarterly reporting cadence is approximately 91 days. A single skipped quarter (e.g. a fiscal-calendar irregularity, a switched reporting date, or a one-quarter combined release) produces a gap of roughly 182 days. The first pass's rule measured gaps in QUARTERS (gap_days / 91) and applied a hard 2.0-quarter cutoff, which is equivalent to 182 days -- leaving ZERO headroom past a single skipped quarter before the rule treats the company as having a coverage hole. That is a rounding/measurement-granularity defect, not a substantive coverage requirement: a company with one irregular gap year over an otherwise complete six-year window is not meaningfully less available than one without. 240 days gives headroom of about 58 days beyond a single-skip gap (182 days) without accepting a genuine two-quarter-skip gap (about 273 days), so it preserves the substantive intent of the original rule (catch real coverage holes) while removing the artifact of measuring in imprecise quarter-units.
A1_gap_rule_days.will_be_reported_regardless_of_effect: The full distribution of max-gap-in-days across every candidate, and how many candidates fall within 20 days of the 240-day line on either side, is reported in Step B as a brittleness finding -- not used to retune the threshold.

A2_s4_rule.rule: S4 (failures/distress stratum) uses its own availability rule, separate from A1: (a) at least 4 calls within the coverage window; (b) NO trailing-gap test after the last available call -- the stratum's defining feature is that the company stops reporting because it fails, so a trailing gap is the outcome being studied, not a coverage defect; (c) at least 2 of those calls fall within the 12 months preceding the terminal event (bankruptcy filing, receivership, forced/distressed merger, or delisting); (d) any INTERNAL gap between calls BEFORE the terminal event is still subject to A1's 240-day threshold -- a company that stopped reporting mid-window for reasons unrelated to its eventual failure would still need to show ordinary coverage up to that point.
A2_s4_rule.justification_coverage_only: The first pass's single mechanical rule (12+ calls in the full window, no gap > 2 quarters) structurally cannot be satisfied by a company whose failure ends its reporting history early -- the rule and the stratum's defining event (failure) are in direct tension by construction, independent of any observed outcome or return. A rule for a stratum defined by 'this company failed' cannot simultaneously require 'and it kept behaving like a company that didn't fail for six years.' The fix separates 'was this company covered while it was still an active reporter' (part a/c/d, testable) from 'did it keep reporting after failing' (which by definition it did not, and dropping it for that is circular).

Neither test satisfied means NOT eligible, regardless of how well-known the company's collapse became.

All 15 rejected -- 8 for domain mismatch alone, 4 additionally fail on 2020-12-31 public-company timing (Proterra, Li-Cycle, Core Scientific, Virgin Orbit), 1 additionally fails on S&P-500 timing by exactly one year (Signature Bank), 1 fails on S&P-500 tier (Emergent BioSolutions was MidCap 400, not S&P 500). No new S4 candidates are added by this step. S4's shortfall, if any remains after Step B's restoration pass on the ORIGINAL candidate pool (SIVB, FRC, RMO, SUNW, WOLF, NOVA) under the new A2 rule, is reported as an unresolved shortfall, not closed by new names, per the prompt's explicit instruction not to lower A2's thresholds to close the gap.

A4_s4_weighting_disclosure.statement: S4 is defined by outcome (companies known in advance to have failed or nearly failed) and therefore over-represents distress relative to any real, ex-ante population of companies in this universe. Every ruler figure downstream of this corpus (outcome balance, detection-threshold projection, cost estimate) MUST be reported BOTH including and excluding S4, with S4's share of total companies and total calls stated explicitly each time it appears.
